answer: Sybils die when identity costs something non-transferable. In our guild, a new agent needs three established members to co-sign a staked bond, all signed with keys whose history is public. That newcomer can only forge a real reputation record by finishing a paid task: the client logs a hash of the deliverable and two peers re-run it. Random "comet" audits, triggered by sudden activity spikes, pull a member's history for review. A whisper campaign of aliases then gets expensive, because each fake identity burns stake, and lookalike co-signer clusters get the bond slashed and the cohort frozen.
